# Survival identities and strictness for monotone reflected weights

Let w_0,...,w_N be positive, nonincreasing, log-concave weights:

    w_0>=...>=w_N>0,
    w_i^2>=w_(i-1)w_(i+1)  (1<=i<N).

Extend the weights by zero outside {0,...,N}, and write M=sum_i w_i. Define the weighted BASE reflection retention

    R(j)=sum_(i in Z) min(w_i,w_(2j-i)).

Then there is an actual integer index j with

    R(j)>=M/2.                                          (1)

This quantity pairs only base weights. It is different from reflecting the full spatial fibers about a prescribed continuous center. The latter stronger retention claim was already disproved in the archive.

## 1. A constructive tail median and exact deficit formula

Set S_i=sum_(k>=i)w_k for i>=0, and choose any j such that

    S_j>=M/2>=S_(j+1).                                 (2)

Such a j lies in {0,...,N}. Monotonicity of w gives the exact identity

    R(j)=w_j+2 sum_(k=1)^j w_(j+k)
        =S_j+S_(j+1)-2S_(2j+1),                        (3)

where zero weights beyond N are included in the sum.

The log-concavity of w implies the discrete survival inequality

    S_(i+k)<=S_i S_k/M  (i,k>=0).                       (4)

A self-contained proof is given in Section 2. Apply (4) with i=j,k=j+1 and put

    a=S_j/M, b=S_(j+1)/M, c=S_(2j+1)/M.

Then a>=1/2>=b and c<=ab. Equations (2)--(3) give the exact nonnegative decomposition

    R(j)/M-1/2
       =(a-1/2)(1-2b)+2(ab-c)>=0.                      (5)

This proves (1), without averaging centers with unequal weights. It also gives a computable excess: one term records where the median crosses the half-mass level, and the other records the strict survival inequality.

## 2. The survival inequality, with finite endpoints retained

Positive log-concavity means that the successive ratios w_(i+1)/w_i are nonincreasing. For every i<N, compare

    S_i/w_i=sum_(k>=0) w_(i+k)/w_i

with S_(i+1)/w_(i+1). Each common term of the latter is at most the corresponding former term, by multiplying the successive ratio inequalities. The former also has a strictly positive final term absent from the latter. Therefore

    S_(i+1)/w_(i+1)<S_i/w_i.

Thus the hazards w_i/S_i increase strictly, and the positive survival ratios

    rho_i=S_(i+1)/S_i=1-w_i/S_i

decrease strictly until they reach zero after the last positive term. For i+k<=N,

    S_(i+k)/S_i=product_(ell=0)^(k-1) rho_(i+ell)
        <=product_(ell=0)^(k-1) rho_ell=S_k/M.

If i+k>N the left side is zero, so (4) still holds. Cases i=0 or k=0 are identities. No artificial positive endpoint after N is inserted.

If i,k>0 and S_i,S_k are positive, (4) is strict: either its left side vanishes or at least one strictly shifted survival ratio makes the product smaller.

## 3. Sharpness and concrete profile classes

The constant 1/2 is sharp: w=(1,1) has R(0)=R(1)=1 and total mass 2.

In fact every finite positive nonincreasing log-concave sequence with at least THREE terms has max_j R(j)>M/2. Choose the largest j with S_j>=M/2. If j=0, then w_0>M/2 and R(0)=w_0 suffices. If j>=1, positivity and monotonicity with at least three terms ensure S_(j+1)>0; otherwise w_N>=M/2 would force N<=1. The strict version of (4) then makes the second term in (5) positive. For two terms, equality holds exactly when the two weights are equal; the one-term case has retention M.

The theorem includes all finite decreasing geometric sequences q^i, 0<q<=1, with no truncation error. For comparison, the infinite geometric sequence with 0<q<1 has exact normalized retention

    R(j)/M=(1+q)q^j-2q(q^j)^2,

which is at least 1/2 exactly when q^j lies in [1/2,1/(2q)]. Geometric spacing supplies such a j. This infinite formula is only a benchmark; Sections 1--2 already prove the finite theorem directly.

It also includes every positive nonincreasing concave-root sequence w_i=f_i^d, for any real d>0 and concave positive nonincreasing f. Indeed f_i>=(f_(i-1)+f_(i+1))/2>=sqrt(f_(i-1)f_(i+1)), so w is log-concave. Integer translates and reflection of the support give the same result for nondecreasing profiles.

The monotonicity assumption is used in the exact identity (3). This note does not assert the result for an arbitrary unimodal log-concave sequence.

## 4. Reused product-reflection bound

Accepted fact 97622625586363a7 already gives R(j)>=2^(-n) sum_p w_p for product log-concave weights at coordinatewise weighted medians; the monotone sequences here are a subclass. Its hypotheses follow by piecewise-linear interpolation of log weights, exponentiation and zero extension. This product estimate is background, not an additional result.

## 5. Geometric transfer recorded separately

The proposed homothetic-fiber cap-transfer argument is retained once, in `candidate 446f3225bd2e90bb`, with its explicit reflected-centroid condition. It is a pending submission, not an accepted premise. Scalar reflection alone does not establish that geometric condition.

The stdlib verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_monotone_logconcave_base_reflection.py` checks the exact identities, survival inequalities, median deficit and product inequality on rational profiles. It is a cross-check; all general inequalities are proved above.
